items.title: Trim verbose defensive coding across all functions
items.intent: Error handling is terse and consistent. Redundant null guards, verbose suggestions, unnecessary fallbacks, single-use variables, and redundant return 0 statements are removed. Saves ~200 lines spread across the entire script.
items.description: Across 82 functions, the script has accumulated verbose patterns: (1) jq calls with 2>/dev/null || true on caller-guaranteed input. (2) Error messages with full command examples belonging in help text. (3) Existence checks on files just created or caller-validated. (4) Multi-line error blocks where single log_error suffices. (5) ~5 redundant return 0 at end of functions. (6) Per-item dual jq calls in enforce_groom_limits and mark_complete that can be combined into single calls. (7) Variables computed and used exactly once that should be inlined. (8) cmd_diagnose has 6 separate jq -r calls on the same file — consolidate to one.
steps: Remove 2>/dev/null from jq calls where input JSON was constructed in the same function
Shorten error messages: remove inline command examples and suggestions
Remove redundant file existence checks where the caller already validated
Collapse multi-line error blocks into single log_error calls
Remove ~5 redundant return 0 at end of functions (load_config, _apply_env_overrides, etc.)
Combine per-item dual jq calls in enforce_groom_limits (id+priority in one call)
Combine two separate jq calls for priority+category in mark_complete into one
Consolidate 6 separate jq -r calls in cmd_diagnose into one jq invocation
Inline single-use variables where the expression is short and clear
Run full test: init, backlog add, backlog list, groom, run --dry-run
acceptanceCriteria: No jq call has 2>/dev/null where input JSON was constructed in the same function
No error message contains a full command example longer than 60 characters
No function ends with a redundant return 0
enforce_groom_limits uses one jq call per item, not two
mark_complete uses one jq call for priority+category, not two
cmd_diagnose uses one jq invocation for initial field extraction, not six
All commands still produce correct error output on bad input
shellcheck passes

items.title: auto silently skips items with missing or too-short intent — no feedback to user
items.intent: When auto-pick bypasses items due to missing or insufficient intent, a warning must be logged identifying each skipped item by ID and stating the reason, so users can fix their backlog.
items.description: pick_item silently skips items where intent is absent or under 20 characters. In an auto session with multiple unready items, the user sees no items processed and no explanation. This makes the intent gate invisible: users don't know why their backlog isn't draining. A targeted log_warn call when each item is bypassed for intent reasons closes the feedback loop.
steps: In pick_item, when an item is rejected due to missing or too-short intent, emit: log_warn "Skipping $id: intent missing or too short (9 chars, need >=20)"
Verify the same path is covered in list_pickable_ids if that function also filters by intent
Run shellcheck and verify no new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Running auto with items whose intent is absent or under 20 chars produces a warning line per skipped item identifying the ID and reason
Items with valid intent are still processed normally — no regression
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
items.groomingNotes: Core UX gap: the intent gate is a hard requirement but invisible when it fires. Users running auto sessions and seeing nothing processed have no way to diagnose why without reading source code. A single log_warn per bypassed item costs nothing and closes the feedback loop completely. Priority should is correct.

items.title: Reduce and refactor the 5000+ line single-file CLI
items.intent: The single-file CLI must be reduced in size and better organized WITHOUT breaking any existing behavior — after 126+ bugs fixed and 40+ features shipped, a refactor that introduces regressions is unacceptable. Every change must be provably safe.
items.description: aishore is 5282 lines in one file, which is intentional for portability. But it has grown organically and contains dead code, verbose defensive patterns, duplicated logic, and oversized functions. Refactor within the single file: extract repeated jq patterns into helpers, collapse verbose guard clauses, remove dead branches (see BUG-072), consolidate duplicated option parsing, and add clear section headers. Goal: reduce to under 4000 lines without losing functionality.
steps: Before any changes, capture baseline output for ALL commands: help, version, status, backlog list, backlog check --all, clean --dry-run, metrics, config check, diagnose — save to a reference file

Audit all functions for dead code: unreachable branches, unused variables, functions never called — remove ONLY after confirming no indirect invocation via eval, variable expansion, or agent callbacks
Identify repeated jq filter patterns and extract into named helper functions — verify each extraction produces identical output by diffing before/after on real backlog data
Collapse verbose guard clauses and defensive patterns that add lines without value (see BUG-072) — but DO NOT remove guards that protect against edge cases discovered in prior bug fixes
Consolidate duplicated option parsing logic across cmd_run, cmd_auto, and cmd_groom — test each command with all flag combinations after consolidation
Merge small single-use utility functions back into their callers ONLY when the function has no semantic value as a named abstraction
Ensure section headers and function grouping follow a logical order: constants, utils, backlog, sprint, groom, review, CLI
After ALL changes, diff baseline output against current output for every command — zero differences allowed
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
Run a full dry-run sprint (aishore run --dry-run) to verify the orchestration path is intact
acceptanceCriteria: The script is under 4500 lines while retaining ALL existing functionality — zero regressions
Every CLI command produces byte-identical output before and after the refactor (verified by baseline diff)
No dead code remains: every function is reachable, every branch is exercised
Repeated jq patterns are consolidated into named helpers
No guards or defensive code from prior bug fixes (BUG-001 through BUG-126) are removed unless provably redundant
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
A dry-run sprint completes without error

items.title: Groom agents silently generate specs repeating known-bad patterns
items.intent: Groom agents must receive proven successful spec examples from the archive alongside failure patterns so they generate specs modeled on what actually works — not just avoiding what failed.
items.description: Groom agents receive failure patterns but no success patterns. Without positive examples, they may generate specs structurally similar to ones that already failed. In run_groom_flow, before invoking groom agents, extract the last 5 successful sprint entries from archive. Format as Specs That Worked with intent, AC, and attempt count. Inject alongside failure patterns.
steps: In run_groom_flow, before invoking groom agents, read last 5 successful entries from backlog/archive/sprints.jsonl
For each successful entry, look up the original item spec from archived backlogs to get intent and AC
Format as a Specs That Worked section with intent, AC count, and attempt count per item
Inject this section into the groom agent prompt alongside the existing failure patterns
When no archive data exists, omit the section entirely
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Groom agents receive a Specs That Worked section showing successful sprint patterns from the archive
Each pattern includes the original intent, AC count, and how many attempts it took
When the archive is empty or has no successes, the section is omitted without error
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
items.groomingNotes: Must priority confirmed. Completes the learning loop started by FEAT-041 — success patterns must reach groom agents, not just the auto session. Dependency on FEAT-041 is correct; sprint only after FEAT-041 passes.
